summary.text: One of the immemorial nine heavens. Year-round winds at strange angles once formed wind knot grass there; fragments later fell into the five regions.

claims.text: No chapter paints green heaven’s landscape as a place entered in these early citations. It is named as one sky level among the immemorial nine.

In The Legends of Ren Zu, the sky of the immemorial antiquity era had nine levels: white heaven, red heaven, orange heaven, yellow heaven, green heaven, azure heaven, blue heaven, purple heaven, and black heaven.
At present, red, orange, yellow, green, azure, blue, and purple heavens are no more, and only white heaven and black heaven remain.

Green heaven is listed among the immemorial nine heavens and is later destroyed with red, orange, yellow, azure, blue, and purple when Ren Zu’s son causes havoc, leaving only white and black heavens alternating between day and night.

Wind knot grass is a round ball-shaped grass lantern. There is none in the five regions; it is a type of grass only found in green heaven of the immemorial nine heavens. Ren Zu’s ten children destroyed the immemorial nine heavens, causing fragments of immemorial green heaven to fall into the five regions. Only in immemorial green heaven would there be winds blowing all year around, at strange directions and angles. Countless plants would be uprooted or shaved until they were bare, and those twigs intertwine in the wind and slowly form into that ball-shaped grass lantern.
